title: August 2026 labor-market conditions combine steady unemployment with uneven establishment growth
source_unit: BLS August 2026 Employment Situation: Current Population Survey household measures and Current Employment Statistics establishment measures

denominator.unit: total nonfarm establishment payroll jobs, not unique workers; exact level not used in this release extraction

total_nonfarm_payroll_change.unit: thousands of jobs, change from July 2026

three_month_average_change.unit: thousands of jobs, June–August 2026 average monthly change

observations.method: BLS seasonally adjusted Current Employment Statistics estimate from the August 2026 Employment Situation release.
observations.uncertainty: August is preliminary and the establishment series is revised; payroll jobs are not unique people and the survey does not identify job quality, control, or AI exposure.
observations.subgroup: Total nonfarm establishments; no worker demographic, occupation, or firm-size subgroup.
observations.counterinterpretation: A positive payroll change can coexist with weak worker bargaining power, unequal access to jobs, involuntary part-time work, or poor job quality.

denominator.unit: thousands of civilian labor force participants age 16 and over, CPS household survey

observations.method: BLS seasonally adjusted Current Population Survey household estimate.
observations.uncertainty: The measure identifies people without a job who meet BLS unemployment criteria; it does not measure underemployment, job quality, control, or all people who want work.
observations.subgroup: All civilians age 16 and over in the CPS labor-force denominator; selected race, age, sex, and education subgroup rates are published separately.
observations.counterinterpretation: An unchanged unemployment rate can conceal shifts in participation, long-term unemployment, involuntary part-time work, or uneven conditions across groups and places.

denominator.unit: thousands of civilian noninstitutional population age 16 and over, CPS household survey

observations.method: BLS seasonally adjusted Current Population Survey household estimate.
observations.uncertainty: Participation and employment-population ratios are population rates, not measures of schedule control, pay adequacy, worker voice, or household security.
observations.subgroup: All civilians age 16 and over; the release reports separate demographic tables.
observations.counterinterpretation: Participation can move for demographic, schooling, care, health, retirement, migration, or discouraged-worker reasons; it should not be read as a single labor-demand signal.

observations.period: August 2026; July and August establishment estimates preliminary where marked

denominator.unit: private nonfarm establishment-survey employees/jobs; exact level not used in this release extraction

average_hourly_earnings.unit: US dollars per hour, seasonally adjusted

average_weekly_earnings.unit: US dollars per week, seasonally adjusted

observations.method: BLS seasonally adjusted Current Employment Statistics hours-and-earnings estimates for all employees on private nonfarm payrolls.
observations.uncertainty: Average earnings are not a worker panel or real-wage measure and do not reveal distribution, benefits, hours across individuals, job security, monitoring, discretion, or bargaining.
observations.subgroup: All employees on private nonfarm payrolls; production and nonsupervisory employees and industry sectors are reported separately.
observations.counterinterpretation: Nominal average pay can rise while purchasing power, hours, benefits, stability, or control worsen; composition and premium-pay changes can move the aggregate.

observations.period: August 2026; seasonally adjusted over-the-month establishment changes

denominator.unit: establishment-survey payroll jobs by selected industry; exact industry levels not used in this release extraction

observations.method: BLS seasonally adjusted CES selected-industry payroll changes from Summary table B.
observations.uncertainty: Industry changes are preliminary where marked and do not show worker transitions, hours, pay distribution, AI exposure, or whether jobs are new, retained, or filled by different workers.
observations.subgroup: Selected private industries; no occupation, worker demographic, establishment-size, union, or geography subgroup in this observation.
observations.counterinterpretation: A sector increase or decrease can reflect seasonality, sampling and benchmark revisions, industry composition, churn, or reclassification rather than a uniform experience for workers in that sector.

denominator.unit: thousands of unemployed people, CPS seasonally adjusted

long_term_unemployed.unit: thousands of people unemployed 27 weeks or more

observations.method: BLS seasonally adjusted Current Population Survey duration-of-unemployment estimate.
observations.uncertainty: Duration is not a measure of cumulative financial loss, benefit receipt, household coping, or future job quality; the August estimate can change with later revisions.
observations.subgroup: Unemployed people age 16 and over; demographic and prior-industry cuts are available in separate tables.
observations.counterinterpretation: Long-term unemployment can have different meanings across age, occupation, health, place, household support, and prior industry; the aggregate share does not identify the mechanism.

related_sources.claim: JOLTS supplies a separate establishment-based openings context through July 2026.
CES series pages supply selected-industry average-hourly-earnings context through August 2026.

boundary: This record places CPS labor-force conditions beside CES payroll, hours, earnings, and industry changes. The household and establishment surveys have different universes; the observations do not identify the same workers, a worker-level causal effect, AI exposure, bargaining power, job quality, household security, or political response. August is a current preliminary publication vintage and should be revisited after revisions.
